<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro primo Regum
<r>1 Reg 15:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Et dixit Samuel ad Saul: Me misit Dóminus, ut úngerem te in regem super pópulum eius Israël; nunc ergo audi vocem Dómini.
<n>2</n> Hæc dicit Dóminus exercítuum: Recénsui quæcúmque fecit Amalec Israéli, quómodo réstitit ei in via, cum ascénderet de Ægýpto.
<n>3</n> Nunc ergo vade et pércute Amalec et demolíre univérsa eius: non parcas ei et non concupíscas ex rebus ipsíus áliquid; sed intérfice a viro usque ad mulíerem et párvulum atque lacténtem, bovem et ovem, camélum et ásinum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Audi, Dómine, hymnum et oratiónem, quam servus tuus orat coram te hódie, ut sint óculi tui apérti, et aures tuæ inténtæ,
* Super domum istam die ac nocte.
<r>℣.</r> Réspice, Dómine, de sanctuário tuo, et de excélso cælórum habitáculo.
<r>℟.</r> Super domum istam die ac nocte.

<n>3</n> Now therefore go, and smite Amalec, and utterly destroy all that he hath: spare him not, nor covet any thing that is his: but slay both man and woman, child and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.

<n>4</n> Præcépit ítaque Saul pópulo, et recénsuit eos quasi agnos: ducénta míllia péditum et decem míllia virórum Iuda.
<n>5</n> Cumque venísset Saul usque ad civitátem Amalec, teténdit insídias in torrénte.
<n>6</n> Dixítque Saul Cinǽo: Abíte, recédite atque descéndite ab Amalec, ne forte invólvam te cum eo; tu enim fecísti misericórdiam cum ómnibus fíliis Israël cum ascénderent de Ægýpto. Et recéssit Cinǽus de médio Amalec.
<n>7</n> Percussítque Saul Amalec ab Hévila donec vénias ad Sur, quæ est e regióne Ægýpti.

* Et malum coram te feci.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: et delíctum meum contra me est semper, quia tibi soli peccávi.

b.b6e4b54bb7:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uintodécimo Kaléndas Iúlii Luna tértia décima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>S</h>ancti Gregorii Barbadici, Cardinalis, Episcopi et Confessoris, cuius dies natalis sequenti die recensetur.
<h>R</h>omæ natális sanctórum ducentórum et sexagínta duórum Mártyrum, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, pro fide Christi sunt necáti, ac pósiti via Salária véteri, ad clivum Cucúmeris.
<h>V</h>esontióne, in Gálliis, sancti Antídii, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui, ob Christi fidem, a Wándalis occísus fuit.
<h>A</h>pollóniæ, in Macedónia, sanctórum Mártyrum Atheniénsium Isáuri Diáconi, Innocéntii, Felícis, Ieremíæ et Peregríni, qui, a Tripóntio Tribúno várie torti, cápite obtruncáti sunt.
<h>T</h>arracínæ, in Campánia, sancti Montáni mílitis, qui, sub Hadriáno Imperatóre et Leóntio Consulári, post multa torménta, martýrii corónam accépit.
<h>A</h>pud Venáfrum, in Campánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Nicándri et Marciáni, qui, in persecutióne Maximiáni, cápite cæsi sunt.
<h>C</h>halcedóne sanctórum Mártyrum Manuélis, Sabélis et Ismaélis, qui, pacis causa apud Iuliánum Apóstatam pro Persárum Rege legatióne fungéntes, ab ipso Imperatóre, cum idóla venerári compelleréntur idque constánti ánimo recusárent, gládio feríri iubéntur.
<h>A</h>mériæ, in Umbria, sancti Himérii Epíscopi, cuius corpus Cremónam, in Insúbria, translátum est.
<h>I</h>n pago Bituricénsi sancti Gundúlphi Epíscopi.
<h>A</h>ureliánis, in Gállia, sancti Avíti, Presbýteri et Confessóris.
<h>I</h>n Phrýgia sancti Hypátii Confessóris.
<h>I</h>tem sancti Bessariónis Anachorétæ.
<h>P</h>isis, in Túscia, sancti Rainerii Confessóris.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.bf739ffdde:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>une 17th 2027, the 13th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>I</h>n England, the holy Abbot Botolph.
<h>A</h>t Rome, two hundred and sixty two holy martyrs, who were slain for Christ's faith's sake in the persecution under Diocletian, and were buried at Cucumber Hill, upon the old Salarian Way.
<h>A</h>t Besançon, in Gaul, the holy martyr Antidius, Bishop of Besançon, who for Christ's faith's sake was slain by the Vandals.
<h>A</h>t Apollonia, in Macedonia, the holy martyrs Isaurus a Deacon, Innocent, Felix, Jeremiah, and Peregrine, Athenians, who were in diverse ways tormented and then beheaded, under the Tribune Tripontius.
<h>A</h>t Tarracina, the holy soldier Montanus, who, after many torments, received the crown of martyrdom under Hadrian the Emperor and Leontius the Consular.
<h>A</h>t Venafro, the holy martyrs Nicander and Marcian, who were beheaded in the persecution under Maximian.
<h>A</h>t Chalcedon, the holy martyrs Manuel, Sabel, and Ishmael. They were envoys who had been sent by the King of Persia to Julian the Apostate to treat for peace. Julian commanded them to worship idols, and, forasmuch as they steadfastly refused so to do, he caused them to be slain with the sword.
<h>A</h>t Amelia, in Umbria, [in the sixth century,] the holy Himerius, Bishop [of that see,] whose body was taken to Cremona, [five hundred years later.]
<h>I</h>n Berry, [also in the sixth century,] holy Gundulph, Bishop [of that see.]
<h>A</h>t Orleans, [in the year 530,] the holy Priest and Confessor Avitus.
<h>I</h>n Phrygia, [in the fifth century,] the holy Confessor Hypatius.

b.f3cb15e77e:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>a nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine: ut et mundi cursus pacífice nobis tuo órdine dirigátur; et Ecclésia tua tranquílla devotióne lætétur.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.7b3add69d9:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, O Lord, we beseech thee, that the course of this world may be so peaceably ordered by thy governance, that thy Church may joyfully serve thee in all godly quietness.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoratio Ss. Quirici and Iulittæ, Martyrum</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Isti sunt Sancti, qui pro Dei amóre minas hóminum contempsérunt: sancti Mártyres in regno cælórum exsúltant cum Angelis. O quam pretiósa est mors Sanctórum, qui assídue assístunt ante Dóminum, et ab ínvicem non sunt separáti!

<r>℣.</r> Mirábilis Deus.
<r>℟.</r> In sanctis suis.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui nos concédis sanctórum Mártyrum tuórum Quírici et Iulíttæ natalítia cólere: da nobis in ætérna beatitúdine de eórum societáte gaudére.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoration of Ss. Quirici and Julittæ, Martyrum</r>
<r>Ant.</r> These are the holy ones who for the love of Christ, recked nothing of the threats of men. In the kingdom of heaven the holy martyrs are filled with joy in the company of Angels. O how precious in the sight of the Lord was the death of these His saints who now stand day and night in His presence and are not divided the one from the other.

<r>℣.</r> Mirábilis Deus.
<r>℟.</r> In sanctis suis.

<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, who dost permit us to keep the birthday of thy holy Martyrs N. and N., grant that we may enjoy their fellowship in everlasting happiness.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
